transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. Thanks for coming in today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Um… work, mostly. I’m a cashier, and I’ve been doing odd things at the register. Like I’ll get stuck tapping the scanner a certain way, or just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. It happened enough that… I got written up last week.
Before you tap the scanner that certain way, do you notice a rising urge or uncomfortable feeling that only goes away once you've done it?

I don’t know if it’s like an urge, exactly. I just… get stuck doing it. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just sort of hanging there over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. It doesn’t really fit what I’m supposed to be doing. It’s gotten me in trouble at work.

During one of these moments when your hand is frozen over the drawer or you're tapping the scanner, are you fully aware of what's happening around you and able to respond if someone speaks to you, or does it feel like you 'blank out' and lose track of time?

I’m… aware enough, I think. I know the customer’s there and that I’m supposed to be moving, but I just get stuck doing the tapping or holding my hand there. It’s not really the right thing for the moment.

When you're tapping the scanner or holding your hand over the drawer, is there a specific worry or fear in your mind that doing it 'correctly' will prevent something bad from happening, or does it just happen without any particular thought behind it?

It’s not really a thought like that. I don’t think I’m preventing something. I just… get stuck doing it, like tapping the scanner or holding my hand there, and it doesn’t fit what’s happening. Then the customer’s waiting, and… yeah, that’s what got me written up.
Have you noticed this kind of repetitive tapping or freezing behavior since you were a child, or is this something that started only recently, as an adult?
No… not since I was a kid. This is more recent. I’d say the voices and those… out-of-place moments have been going on maybe three months or so.
You mentioned hearing voices - can you tell me more about that? What do the voices say, and how often do you hear them?

Most days, I guess. It sounds like… a couple people talking just off to the side of me. Sometimes they say my name, like from the stockroom, or say I rang something up wrong. But when I look, there’s nobody there. And other people don’t seem to hear it.
Do you have any medical conditions, recent illnesses, head injuries, or are you using any medications, drugs, or alcohol that started around the same time these symptoms began?
I don’t really know. Nothing I can think of that started then. I mean… I’m not aware of any head injury or illness around that time. As far as medications or anything, nothing new comes to mind.

Besides the tapping and freezing at the register, have you noticed times when your body becomes very stiff or rigid, when you stop talking altogether, or when someone tries to move your arm and it feels like it stays in that position?

Not really like that, I don’t think. It’s more… at the register I get stuck doing something that doesn’t make sense right then. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. It happened enough that I got written up last week.
Aside from the voices, have you had any strong beliefs lately that others might be watching you, plotting against you, or trying to control your actions?
I don’t know… not really. I mean, sometimes I feel uncomfortable, like people are looking at me, but I wouldn’t say they’re plotting or controlling me. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you noticed any times recently when you felt confused, disoriented about where you were or what day it was, or unusually drowsy or 'foggy' in your thinking?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get distracted sometimes, but I haven’t been lost about where I am or what day it is. Not unusually drowsy, either.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any neurological conditions, such as seizures, epilepsy, or thyroid problems, or has a doctor ever mentioned anything unusual on a brain scan or blood test?
No… not that I know of. I don’t think anyone’s ever told me there was something like that.

Have you noticed any changes in your emotions or motivation lately—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, showing less emotion on your face, or wanting to withdraw from friends and family?

Yeah… I guess so. I still care about my wife and kids, it’s not that I don’t. I just… don’t have much push lately. Like I should call my son at college, or go meet the kayak group, or work on little repair projects at home, and I just don’t.

When people ask what’s wrong, I mostly just shrug. I can’t really find much to say.
Have you or others noticed that your speech sometimes becomes hard to follow—like jumping between unrelated topics, or losing the thread of what you're trying to say?
I’m not sure. I don’t really notice it myself. Maybe I lose my train of thought sometimes, but… I don’t think I jump around a lot.
How long have you been feeling this lack of motivation and reduced emotional expression—did it start around the same time as the voices about three months ago, or has it been going on longer?
Longer, I think. It didn’t start with the voices. It’s been… building for maybe a little over two years, since my youngest left the Eastern Shore for college.
